recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if HL7 creates a formal Workflow work group that can own resources or a later final Jira decision transfers PlanDefinition ownership away from CDS.
issue_request: FHIR-11148 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU2 request to move PlanDefinition from the Clinical Decision Support work group to the workflow work group because PlanDefinition supports broad workflow, protocol, order set, and non-CDS use cases.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentions FHIR-11148. The Jira comment says PlanDefinition was recategorized as Workflow by Lloyd's changes. The applied related issue FHIR-10683 was implemented in SVN 11382 / git bd1507dafa96568bf37503ff029bbabe8c3d8be2, adding PlanDefinition prose that identifies it as a FHIR Workflow definition resource.
additional_context: FHIR-11148's approved resolution did not transfer resource ownership; it states Workflow was a task force rather than a work group that could own resources, and that CDS would coordinate with that task force. FHIR-11232 made the same request for PlanDefinition and ActivityDefinition and had the same resolution and application comments. FHIR-14447 later records continued Workflow report alignment work for CDS resources.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active current source keeps PlanDefinition assigned to CDS in fhir.ini and the StructureDefinition wg extension, while the PlanDefinition introduction and Workflow page already present PlanDefinition as part of the Workflow definition pattern.

related_jiras.note: Applied the broader decision that CDS resources should follow and declare Workflow patterns, including PlanDefinition as a Definition resource.
Made the same work-group ownership request for PlanDefinition and ActivityDefinition and received the same resolution.
Later Workflow report alignment issue confirms continued CDS-owned workflow-pattern alignment work rather than an ownership transfer.
